clue.text: One relatively likely to succeed.

definitions.text: One relatively likely to succeed.

parts.note: 'relatively' means by family relation: a relative expected to inherit a title unless a closer heir is born

explanation.definitionFit: A family member who will inherit a title or throne unless someone with a stronger claim appears.

clue.text: A'lovely, collection, but not open public.

definitions.text: A'lovely, collection, but not open public.

parts.words: A'lovely, collection, but not open public
parts.note: a gathering of beautiful women kept in private quarters that outsiders may not enter

explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of a Muslim household, closed to visitors, and the wives or concubines living there.

clue.text: Tense as a remark asserting excellence be

definitions.text: Tense
definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense for continuing or unfinished past action

definitions.text: a remark asserting excellence
definitions.meaning: split as ..., a boast of flawlessness

explanation.surface: Someone becomes tense when told to live up to their own claim of excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'be' looks like a stray from the newspaper print and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperfect is the past tense of unfinished action, and split in two the word is a boast of flawlessness.

clue.text: Good days, arboreally speaking.

definitions.text: Good days, arboreally speaking.

parts.note: prosperous times described in tree language, as if full of palm trees

explanation.definitionFit: Palmy days are flourishing, prosperous times, and the word literally means full of palm trees.

clue.text: If banged about, it might certainly Abe yell.

definitions.text: it

indicators.note: when knocked around, the letters of the words given form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone named Abe yells after taking a knock to the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banged about' rearranges ABE YELL; the answer is 'it', the organ that would make Abe yell if hit.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' points at the organ of sight, the thing that hurts when struck.

clue.text: One of their jobs is to usher people out.

definitions.text: One of their jobs is to usher people out.

parts.words: One of their jobs is to usher people out
parts.note: officials whose duties include giving players out, as in cricket, rather than showing guests to the door

explanation.definitionFit: Sports officials, who in cricket rule batsmen out with a raised finger.

clue.text: Ring changes (but not to grin!)

definitions.text: Ring changes (but not to grin!)

parts.note: a sequence of bell changes, and in the bracket a burst of laughter that is more than a grin

explanation.definitionFit: Change ringing produces a sequence of bells, and a burst of laughter goes by the same word.

clue.text: It seems a very hard way of speaking.

definitions.text: It seems a very hard way of speaking.

parts.words: It seems a very hard way of speaking
parts.note: a manner of speech saying the opposite of what is meant, which also looks like an adjective for something like iron

explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what one means, a word that also reads as 'like iron', very hard.

clue.text: Can't net me anyhow this statute.

definitions.text: statute

indicators.note: means in any old way, so the letters are put down in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a new law somehow fails to catch the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges CAN'T NET ME; 'this' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A law passed by a legislature is a statute, a formally enacted measure.

clue.text: In the matter of seed it's a set-back.

definitions.text: set-back

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning concerning, as in business letters
pulses are the edible seeds of peas, beans and lentils

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that the seed crop has suffered a reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back an attack, a rebuff or check, is a set-back for the attacker.

clue.text: As a player no more than automatic.

definitions.text: As a player no more than automatic.

parts.words: As a player no more than automatic
parts.note: a keyboard instrument that plays itself from a perforated roll, not a sportsman going through the motions

explanation.definitionFit: The player piano, worked mechanically from a paper roll with no pianist needed.

clue.text: This Andrew's a real clown,

definitions.text: This Andrew's a real clown,

parts.note: the word that goes before Andrew in the old phrase for a buffoon or jester

explanation.definitionFit: A merry-andrew is a clown or buffoon, once a mountebank's assistant.

clue.text: Measure taken by knights abroad.

definitions.text: Measure
taken by knights abroad
definitions.meaning: the port in the Holy Land captured by Crusader knights

explanation.surface: Crusading knights conquer a patch of foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area, and the Levant port captured by Richard the Lionheart's Crusaders.

clue.text: Noisy type of Indian in the field?

definitions.text: Noisy type of Indian in the field?

parts.words: Noisy type of Indian in the field?
parts.note: an Indian peasant farmer, whose name is said like a noisy disturbance

explanation.definitionFit: In British India a ryot was a peasant cultivator, and the word is said like riot, an uproar.

clue.text: "And of mind, all passion spent "(Milton).

definitions.text: "And of mind, all passion spent "(Milton).

parts.note: a gap in the last line of Milton's Samson Agonistes, filled by a word for peacefulness

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Milton's line means serene, untroubled, at peace after passion is spent.

definitions.text: With which to 'arrange the rice in Madras?

parts.words: With which to 'arrange the rice in Madras?
parts.note: a groom's tool for a horse's coat, read jokingly as a comb for tidying an Indian dish

explanation.definitionFit: A metal-toothed comb for grooming horses, to curry being to groom, and also a comb for a spicy Madras dish.

clue.text: One way to save face.

definitions.text: One way to save face.

parts.note: a covering literally keeps the face hidden, rather than preserving one's dignity

explanation.definitionFit: A fine fabric covering hiding the face, taking 'save face' literally.

clue.text: Horticulturally acquired maybe from golden Kew.

definitions.text: Horticulturally acquired maybe from golden Kew.

indicators.note: as a gardener would bed things out afresh, the letters are cultivated into a new order

explanation.surface: Learning picked up in the famous London botanical gardens.

clue.text: First process of abandonment at sea.

definitions.text: First process of abandonment at sea.

parts.words: First process of abandonment at sea
parts.note: rodents are said to be the first to desert a sinking ship, and the word also means deserting a cause

explanation.definitionFit: Deserting one's side, named after rodents leaving a doomed vessel first.

clue.text: No scarcity it would seem and doesn't he like it

definitions.text: No scarcity it would seem and doesn't he like it

parts.words: No scarcity it would seem and doesn't he like it
parts.note: the word splits into a surplus and a great weight, an excess that the greedy eater enjoys

explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater: the word splits into a surplus plus a large weight, plenty that such a person relishes.

clue.text: .Worthless, one would think, to an sailor.

definitions.text: .Worthless, one would think, to an sailor.

parts.words: .Worthless, one would think, to an sailor
parts.note: a small harbour craft selling provisions to ships, whose name opens with a slang word for useless

explanation.definitionFit: A small boat that brings goods to ships at anchor, its name starting with slang for worthless.

clue.text: Taken daily of course by the Yeomen of the Guard.

definitions.text: Taken daily of course by the Yeomen of the Guard.

parts.words: Taken daily of course by the Yeomen of the Guard
parts.note: the guards at the Tower of London are nicknamed for eating ox meat, so a hot meat broth suits them

explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard, ceremonial royal guards, are popularly called Beefeaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot broth made from ox meat, joked to be the drink of the Beefeaters.

clue.text: Zigzags forward, but will swing back.

definitions.text: Zigzags

indicators.note: the word for swing is read in the backward direction

parts.note: to sway is to swing from side to side

explanation.surface: A ship's motion, veering forward and then rolling the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that deviates from its course side to side is zigzagging.

clue.text: "The earth hath bubbles as the has" (Macbeth).

definitions.text: "The earth hath bubbles as the has" (Macbeth).

parts.words: "The earth hath bubbles as the has" (Macbeth)
parts.note: Banquo's line about the witches has a missing word, the liquid of seas and rivers

explanation.definitionFit: Banquo compares the vanishing witches to the bubbles found in the sea or a stream.

clue.text: The dandy's a failure at the very outset.

definitions.text: The dandy's a failure at the very outset.

parts.words: The dandy's a failure at the very outset
parts.note: a word for a fop whose opening letters spell a word for a flop

explanation.definitionFit: A fop or swell, and the word's first three letters spell a failure.

clue.text: Just pass, that high ball back to us

definitions.text: Just pass

indicators.note: the word for the high ball is turned to read the other way

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in tennis or cricket
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal. 'Just pass' is the definition: a bolus is a lump of food or a pill small enough to swallow in one go.

clue.text: Get all hot on the trail?

definitions.text: Get all hot
definitions.meaning: to burn fiercely or flare up in anger

definitions.text: on the trail?
definitions.meaning: a mark cut on a tree to show a path

explanation.surface: A tracker grows heated when close behind the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn fiercely, and a mark slashed on trees to show a path, as in blazing a trail.

clue.text: We are undoubtedly in the right set here.

definitions.text: We are undoubtedly in the right set here.

indicators.note: the word we is placed inside the word set, splitting it after its first letter

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied clique sure it belongs among the right people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the whole clue reads as smug approval of the company kept, which the answer expresses.

clue.text: Hot stuff — quite overwhelming at times.

definitions.text: Hot stuff — quite overwhelming at times.

parts.words: Hot stuff — quite overwhelming at times
parts.note: molten rock from a volcano, which can bury whole towns, not an attractive person

clue.text: One who seems to have had the chuck.

definitions.text: One who seems to have had the chuck.

parts.words: One who seems to have had the chuck
parts.note: someone rejected by society, as if thrown away, 'the chuck' being slang for dismissal

clue.text: How senseless to welt Dad like this!

definitions.text: How senseless to welt Dad like this!

indicators.note: points to the letters given being rearranged into the form the answer takes

explanation.walkthrough: 'like this' signals the rearrangement of WELT DAD, and the result is a word for nonsense, matching 'How senseless'.

clue.text: Might one expect a profit from briefs here?

definitions.text: Might one expect a profit from briefs here?

parts.words: Might one expect a profit from briefs here?
